sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: The candidate faithfully encodes the complete DIRECT_STATIC conditional requirement: it targets ships, uses the required ship-owned paths and datatypes, guards all antecedent inputs within the A/B applicability branch, and reports violations only when approval is not Approved or the certificate-entry boolean is not true. Non-applicable ships impose no consequence constraint, and deterministic validation is valid.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Repair the applicability alternatives: the candidate only treats category C as the non-applicable category, so a ship with any other non-A/B category can fail even though the implication is false and the requirement imposes no approval or certificate constraint. Encode the applicability as a single conditional implication whose non-applicable branch covers every category not in {A,B} (or enforce the canonical exhaustive A/B/C controlled-value domain before using category C), while retaining the required ship-owned inputs and both consequences for the applicable branch.

The conditional SPARQL violation test correctly limits the consequences to the A/B antecedent, but the unconditional sh:minCount 1 constraints on constructionDate, carriedNoxiousLiquidSubstanceRequiresType3Tank, and cargoTankType make non-applicable ships fail merely because antecedent inputs are absent. Remove unconditional existence constraints from conditional applicability inputs, or encode their presence only within the applicable antecedent; retain the ship-owned paths and both applicable consequences. The prior applicability instruction remains applicable: ensure the non-applicable branch covers every category outside {A,B}, not only an assumed Category C.

Preserve the prior applicability and conditional-input instructions. The SPARQL violation logic is reversed: FILTER(NOT EXISTS {antecedent} || NOT EXISTS {antecedent plus consequences}) rejects non-applicable ships and can create accidental failures. Replace it with a guarded implication: identify only ships whose category is A or B and whose construction date, NLS boolean, and cargo-tank type satisfy the antecedent, then report a violation only when the Administration approval is not evidenceStateApproved or applicableCertificatePolarOperationEntryPresent is not true. Ships outside categories A and B must impose no such constraint, and do not add unconditional minCount constraints for the antecedent inputs.

The candidate faithfully encodes the complete DIRECT_STATIC conditional requirement: it targets ships, uses the required ship-owned paths and datatypes, guards all antecedent inputs within the A/B applicability branch, and reports violations only when approval is not Approved or the certificate-entry boolean is not true. Non-applicable ships impose no consequence constraint, and deterministic validation is valid.
